endorsements.quote: Promote equity and language inclusivity by thoroughly testing all languages used in the health system’s MAT workflow
Design comprehensive training modules for translation teams on LLM limitations and mitigation strategies

Translators should be trained to recognize the common pitfalls (e.g., hallucinations, context loss, bias) of LLMs in MAT, and, to counteract human overreliance, translators could be intermittently prompted to justify their choice to leave a sentence unedited in a translation, similar to safety checks in electronic health records (EHRs) for potential medication-medication interactions 33 .
Implement features prompting users to justify non-edits, similar to EHR clinical decision support
LLM-based MAT should follow selective deployment beginning with note types and languages that have been shown to perform well in prospective pilot studies.
Reinforce a translator-in-the-loop model that emphasizes LLM outputs should be a first draft with the final review remaining the translator’s responsibility

Each translation request should log a unique identifier, timestamp, LLM used, the model’s initial translation, the final version, note type, target language, translator ID, flags for harmful outputs, and metrics such as generation and editing times.
Ensure transparency regarding the use of AI in translating patient documents

Success should be defined by practical outcomes, such as faster translation turnaround times, higher user satisfaction (both for translators and patients), and improved patient outcomes, rather than technical metrics alone.

Operational metrics: Translation turnaround time and the proportion of patients with NELP who receive language-concordant discharge instructions should be used to measure system efficiency, pinpoint areas for workflow refinement, and ensure equitable care delivery across diverse language groups.
Regulatory bodies, like the Joint Commission, should extend their evaluations to examine whether MAT meets the same standards required for traditional translation methods
Patient advisory boards can be leveraged to collect direct patient feedback on clarity and acceptability of translations

unlisted_practices: Use zero-data-retention endpoints or private LLM instances so that closed-source LLMs never expose PHI through unprotected APIs.
Scrub fine-tuning datasets of PHI using de-identification tools before fine-tuning translation models.
Integrate LLM machine-assisted translation into translators' existing EHR and CAT-tool workflows.
Co-design MAT prompts, interfaces, and error-check features with translators and clinicians.
Conduct retrospective testing on offline data after LLM changes or workflow updates and before live deployment.
Pilot MAT with small-scale prospective rollouts for one language or document type before expanding.
Periodically assess MAT translation quality using frameworks such as MQM on representative samples with manual evaluation by the translation team.
Evaluate patient understandability and actionability of translations using PEMAT or patient comprehension questions administered by patients or patient advisory boards.
Monitor clinical outcomes such as readmission and mortality among patients with non-English language preference to gauge MAT effects.
Preserve a translator-in-the-loop model and maintain human review of machine-generated translations before they reach patients.
Negotiate contracts requiring third-party translation vendors to refine MAT drafts rather than translate from scratch.
Regulators and HHS should update CLAS standards and revise Section 1557 to set LLM baseline qualifications, acceptable error rates, data privacy safeguards, and language-specific requirements.
Build a shared de-identified clinical translation corpus across health systems, including digitally underrepresented languages, for fine-tuning and benchmarking.
Use a preparation prompt to clean up poorly structured clinical notes before translation, and encourage clinicians to write high-quality discharge summaries.
Fine-tune MAT models on translator-approved data, targeting challenging languages and note types first.

screen.reason: This is a framework/roadmap paper providing implementation guidance and recommendations for healthcare leaders and policymakers on operationalizing machine-assisted translation using LLMs.
